newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close lower, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close lower, seen firm.

text.p: Argentine stocks staged a technical pullback Tuesday but were seen firm in the near-term, dealers said.

"This was a technical correction driven by sharp falls in a handful of stocks, some of which recently announced weak quarterly results," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli. "But the bolsa should bounce back quickly provided the markets remain stable in New York."
The blue-chip MerVal index dropped 2.1 percent to 726.77, wiping out Monday's gains, while the broad market shed 1.1 percent.
Floor volume picked up to 29.1 million pesos from 23.9 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals swelled to 140.2 million pesos from 108.5 million Monday.
"Yesterday the market rose with weak volume which set the stage for today's retreat," said Dario Lizzano, head of research at Banco Santander.
He predicted prices would consolidate at these levels and head for a target of 760, where the MerVal stalled in February.
Losing stocks in the session smashed winners 42 to 12 and nine issues closed unchanged.

The day's worst main-tier performer was carmaker Ciadea, which dived 8.3 percent both on last Thursday's lower-than-expected quarterly profit and on news of factory stoppages this month blamed on a shortage of supplies and changes in export plans, dealers said.
Construction stock Polledo tumbled 6.1 percent and oil company Astra dropped 6.1 percent.
Top MerVal gainers were electricity generators Central Costanera and Central Puerto, both up 0.9 percent, and holding company Comercial del Plata, up 0.6 percent.
